source:
Create a massive, seamless 3D Open-World RPG map divided into 4 hyper-detailed mega-biomes, connected by a central neutral hub called "The Nexus Palace".

Zone 1 (Cyberpunk Metropolis): A dense neon-lit futuristic city. Add towering skyscrapers with holographic advertisements, drivable hover-car lanes in the sky, dark rainy asphalt streets with puddle reflections, and accessible underground cyberpunk slums filled with neon signs and rusty pipes.
Zone 2 (Mystical Luminescent Forest): A fantasy forest where everything glows. Generate giant ancient trees with glowing purple leaves, bioluminescent rivers flowing with neon blue water, interactive glowing mushrooms that boost player jump height, and dense volumetric fog floating between the trees.
Zone 3 (Scrapyard Wasteland): A post-apocalyptic diesel-punk desert. Fill it with moving sandstorms, massive rusted metal shipwrecks, turning mechanical gears half-buried in the sand, and abandoned scavenger outposts made of iron sheets.
Zone 4 (Celestial Floating Kingdom): A majestic realm of sky islands. Design white marble castles with gold trims, floating waterfalls that drop water into the endless sky, moving cloud 
platforms for parkour, and ancient Greek-style temples.

Implement an advanced, fluid, and responsive 3D movement and Combat System for all players.
Movement Mechanics: Enable smooth wall-running on flat vertical surfaces, a tactical double-dash with motion blur effects, a grappling hook system that attaches to any metal or wooden structure, and a ledge-climbing mechanic.
Combat Core: Build a hybrid combat system (Melee and Ranged). Melee weapons (like Laser Katanas and Greatswords) must have a 3-hit combo animation system with camera-shake on impact and directional slashing visual effects. Ranged weapons (like Plasma Rifles and Magic Staffs) must feature over-the-shoulder aiming, custom particle projectiles, projectile drop, and localized hitboxes (Headshot = 2.5x damage).
Class Skill Trees: Implement 3 distinct classes (Cyber-Ninja, Arch-Mage, and Wasteland Juggernaut), each with 5 unique unlockable active skills containing custom particle VFX.
Populate the map with smart Al enemies and 4 massive World Bosses,

.one for each biome

Minion Al: Enemies must use pathfinding to chase players, take cover behind walls when low on health, and alert nearby allies when

.engaged in combat

Cyber Metropolis Boss ("Mecha-Titan Prime"): A 50-foot-tall robot

that spawns in the city center. It shoots tracking homing missiles, slams the ground creating a massive expanding shockwave ring that players must jump over, and enters a shield-overcharge phase

.at 30% health

Floating Kingdom Boss ("Aether Dragon"): A massive flying dragon that circles the sky castles. It breathes holy fire that coats platforms in damaging light, creates tornadoes that push players off the floating islands, and requires players to use their grappling hooks to .board its back to deal critical damage

Script a global dynamic 24-minute Day/Night cycle combined with a .randomized Weather Engine that alters gameplay
Day/Night Cycle: Transition smoothly between a bright sunny day with God-rays, a golden hour sunset, and a pitch-black midnight .where players require flashlights or glowing gear to see
Dynamic Weather: Randomly trigger 4 weather events: Heavy Acid Rain in the Cyberpunk City (deals slowly chipping armor damage over time), Magic Mana Storm in the Forest (amplifies magic damage by 50% and changes sky color to purple), Sandstorm in the Wasteland (reduces player visibility to 15 studs and slows movement speed), and Thunderstorms in the Floating Kingdom (lightning bolts strike random spots on the map, causing instant .death if hit)

Create a comprehensive RPG data-store, inventory, and user interface framework.
UI Layout: Design a clean, modern, and minimalist sci-fi/fantasy hybrid GUI. Include a circular health and mana bar in the bottom center, a mini-map in the top-right showing quest markers and player locations, and a neat clean side-menu for Inventory, Skills, and Quests.
Loot & Inventory: Build a color-coded rarity system for drops (Common=White, Rare=Blue, Epic=Purple, Legendary=Gold). Items must drop from defeated enemies as physical glowing 3D crates that players can walk over to collect. Implement a full Inventory screen with weapon equipping slots and stat displays.
Data Persistence: Ensure all player data (Level, Gold, Gems, Equipped Items, Skill Tree Points) saves automatically using Roblox DataStoreService every 60 seconds and upon leaving the server.

answers.ask: You asked for a seamless world but also for four mega-biomes - should these generate as one continuous surface, or as four maps stitched at the hub?
answers.answer: Build it as one continuous seamless surface, with the four biomes naturally connected around The Nexus Palace at the center.

answers.ask: The hub sits between four clashing themes - should the Nexus Palace read as neutral stone, or borrow from one of the biomes?
answers.answer: The Nexus Palace should use a neutral majestic stone-and-marble style with subtle gold accents, distinct from all four biome themes.

answers.ask: Assumed region scale, over 2000 studs - how long should crossing one biome on foot take?
answers.answer: Target roughly 3–5 minutes to cross a biome on foot; keep the first build compact enough to remain playable while still feeling large.

answers.ask: Do players build their own bases anywhere in the world, or is all progression through levels, loot and skill trees?
answers.answer: No player base-building is called for; progression is through levels, loot, equipment, quests, and skill trees.

## Enriched image prompt
Create one seamless open-world RPG surface with four large biomes naturally connected around The Nexus Palace at the center. Make the palace a neutral majestic stone-and-marble safe hub with subtle gold accents. In the Cyberpunk Metropolis, arrange dense rainy streets, neon signs, towering skyscrapers, holographic advertisements, elevated hover-car lanes, and accessible underground slums with rusty pipes; reserve the city center for a 50-foot robot boss encounter. Build the Mystical Luminescent Forest from giant ancient trees with glowing purple leaves, neon-blue bioluminescent rivers, glowing jump mushrooms, and fog between the trunks. Fill the Scrapyard Wasteland with desert ground, massive rusted shipwrecks, half-buried turning gears, iron-sheet scavenger outposts, and a broad boss arena. Form the Celestial Floating Kingdom from sky-island clusters, white marble castles with gold trim, Greek-style temples, floating waterfalls, moving cloud platforms, and an aerial arena around the castles for a huge dragon boss. Give every biome one distinct world-boss encounter area and routes suitable for wall-running, ledge climbing, dashing, and grappling to metal or wood. Keep each biome roughly 3–5 minutes across on foot and visually connect all four to the central palace.

## Genre
The dominant genre is RPG because levels, loot, quests, skill trees, classes, combat, enemies, and world bosses define the game. The exploratory world supports that RPG loop without requiring a second genre.

## Shape and preset
Use `world-open-biomes` for four distinct regions around the Nexus. Override its usual separate-map route: the author explicitly requires one continuous seamless surface. No preset is a clean match because the open-biome preset assumes survival resources and player base-building, which the author explicitly rejected.

## Config requirements
Use `safezone-town` and `social-hub` for The Nexus Palace; `hazard-aggro` for four boss encounter grounds; `landmark-focal` for the palace, city towers, shipwrecks, and sky castles; universal `settlement-density` for the metropolis; `path-road-vehicle` as non-course elevated hover-car streets; `water-body` for the forest rivers and floating waterfalls; `island-cluster` for the Celestial Kingdom; `obstacle-moving` for the cloud platforms; and universal `terrain-relief` for the four-region landform transitions. Do not include `buildzone-plot`.

## Layout requirements
Place `spawner-npc` emitters in separated enemy grounds and exactly four boss origins, one per biome; the Cyberpunk origin is in the city center and the Celestial origin circles the sky castles, while the two unnamed bosses receive only grounded arena origins. Place `powerup-buffs` on the interactive glowing mushrooms in the forest. Ambient weather, combat, classes, UI, data persistence, and dynamic enemy behavior are mechanics, not placements.

## Layout components
The containing world has a central palace hub and four named surrounding zones: Cyberpunk Metropolis, Mystical Luminescent Forest, Scrapyard Wasteland, and Celestial Floating Kingdom. Roads, natural trails, bridges, and elevation changes join every biome directly to the Nexus without loading transitions. Preserve all named city, forest, wasteland, and sky-island landmarks and one boss ground per zone. Frame the palace as the center of the composition with the four themes reading as distinct quadrants.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: the seamless four-way connectivity and boss-ground separation must be authoritative before the biome-specific isometric dressing.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge because four 3–5-minute-crossing biomes must coexist, although the first build should stay as compact as that traversal target permits. The theme deliberately combines neon cyberpunk, luminescent fantasy forest, diesel-punk wasteland, celestial marble-and-gold fantasy, and a neutral palace. `P2` covers elevated lanes, underground layers, floating islands, and cloud platforms; `P3` covers surface-to-underground slum transitions; and `CHECK` covers rivers, waterfalls, and open-air island traversal. The shape's normal `P4` is explicitly overridden to a continuous map.
